children: SpaceX’s

growing presence in major stock indexes has had little effect on their valuations or performance, despite concerns ahead of its record initial public offering, Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider said.
Nearly five months after the offering, roughly a third of SpaceX

shares are available for public trading, up from 5% at its debut. That increase has lifted its weight in several benchmarks and expanded ownership by funds that track them, Snider and his colleagues wrote in a Nov. 6 report.

image.alt: Sample of large IPOs with low float includes 14 IPOs with deal values equating to at least 0.05% of Russell 3000 market cap at the time of IPO and float shares representing less than 10% of total.

children: For index investors, the findings suggest SpaceX’s
addition has made relatively little difference to their portfolios’ overall characteristics. Goldman’s analysis found only small changes in the Nasdaq-100’s
valuation, volatility and concentration when comparing the index with and without the stock.
Nasdaq-100 effects remain modest
SpaceX
accounts for about 2.5% of the Nasdaq-100
, its largest weighting among major U.S. equity indexes examined in the report.
The index trades at 19.5 times expected earnings over the next 12 months. Excluding SpaceX
, that multiple would fall to 19.2 times, Goldman calculated.
Since SpaceX
joined the benchmark, the Nasdaq-100
has declined 10.3%. Without the company, the decline would have been 10%. Annualized volatility, a measure of price fluctuations, was also only slightly higher with SpaceX included.
The index’s 10 largest holdings account for 50% of its value under either calculation. Its 20 largest holdings represent 67%, compared with 64% without SpaceX
Index rebalances could spur buying
Passive exchange-traded funds held roughly $30 billion of SpaceX
shares at the end of October, according to the report. About $20 billion was held by funds tracking the Nasdaq-100 (NCX).
Further increases in publicly tradable shares should lift ownership by index funds. Goldman estimated that about half of SpaceX
shares would become available for public trading by mid-2027 as restrictions on existing shareholders expire.

Scheduled index adjustments could generate additional demand before then. Goldman estimated that rebalancing the Russell 1000 Growth Index using the report’s current figures would trigger more than $10 billion in buying by passive ETFs tracking the benchmark. Its next scheduled rebalance is Dec. 11.
The mechanical effect on SpaceX’s Nasdaq-100
weighting should be smaller because of the benchmark’s rules for companies with a limited public float, the report said.
S&P 500 entry could wait until 2027
SpaceX
remains outside the S&P 500 (
). Goldman said the index’s eligibility requirements point to potential inclusion in the second half of 2027.

Under the rules described in the report, companies must have been publicly traded for at least 12 months. They must also report positive net income from continuing operations under standard accounting rules for the latest quarter and the latest four quarters combined.
Based on consensus earnings forecasts, SpaceX
would meet the profitability requirement after reporting second-quarter 2027 results. It would likely have satisfied the trading-history requirement by then as well.
A merger with an existing S&P 500 (
) member could offer another route, Goldman said. Such membership changes are reviewed individually, leaving the timing of any inclusion uncertain.

title: SpaceX has had limited impact on stock indexes, Goldman Sachs says
